events.text_en: A month before Kim Cốc Viên falls, Kim Vạn Lý sells his share of its notes to the banker Quản Doanh Hư.
In Vật Hoa Thị the ruined banker Quản Doanh Hư sells four copies of Kim Cốc Viên's Golden Valley Ledger Canon to pay his creditors.
Quản Doanh Hư dies in a rented room in Vật Hoa Thị with eighty parts in a hundred paid; his ledger is closed.
Mẫn Tế Thế, the healer of Hạnh Hoa Thị, spends his last years in needles to break a fever in the lamp-makers' quarter and dies under the apricot tree.
Bào Thừa Phong of Yên Ba dies owing for his son's new yards; Kim Vạn Lý pays the debt for a third of the ship-house.
Quản Phục Thu opens her grandfather's closed ledger and takes on the last twenty parts of the Kim Cốc debt.
Kim Vạn Lý orders three hulls from the Bào yards, deep-keeled and copper-sheathed for southern water, and lends them to Thúy Vi's port house.
